chunks: And ʿAlī ibn Abī Ḥamzah narrated from Abū Baṣīr, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:

“The Tawrah was revealed on six nights having passed of the month of Ramadan, and the Injīl was revealed on twelve having passed of the month of Ramadan, and the Zabūr was revealed on the night of eighteen of the month of Ramadan, and the Qur’an [al-Furqān] was revealed on Laylat al-Qadr.”

key_terms.التَّوْرَاةُ: The Torah, a divinely revealed scripture
key_terms.الزَّبُورُ: The Psalms, the scripture given to a prophet
key_terms.الْإِنْجِيلُ: The Gospel, a divinely revealed scripture
key_terms.الْفُرْقَانُ: A name of the Qur’an meaning the criterion that distinguishes truth from falsehood
key_terms.الْقُرْآنُ: The Qur’an, the final divine revelation
key_terms.شَهْرِ رَمَضَانَ: The month of Ramadan, a sacred month associated with revelation and fasting
key_terms.لَيْلَةِ الْقَدْرِ: The Night of Decree, the blessed night in which the Qur’an was revealed

ai.seo_question: When were the Tawrah, Injīl, Zabūr, and Qur’an revealed in the month of Ramadan?
ai.summary: This hadith states the times in Ramadan at which major divine scriptures were revealed: the Tawrah, the Injīl, the Zabūr, and the Qur’an. It highlights the sanctity of the month of Ramadan and the special status of Laylat al-Qadr as the night of the Qur’an’s revelation.
